summary.headline: EPACK Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR886 crore (+34% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 6.21% from 8.24% as PLI income dropped to nil.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose about 34% YoY to INR886 crore, the company's highest quarterly revenue, with RAC up about 44% (roughly 30% volume, 14% value). EBITDA was INR55 crore, up about 0.7% YoY, with margin at 6.21% versus 8.24%; management said the prior-year figure included INR13.31 crore of PLI income, and the like-for-like underlying margin was about 6.4% in Q1 FY26. Net profit was INR11.8 crore, and management cited a forex loss of about INR6-7 crore and higher wage costs as pressures. Management said FY27 is the last year of PLI benefit and is rolling back PLI discounts shared with brand customers, aiming to fully reverse them by year-end.

segments.name: RAC (room air conditioners)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR660 crore of the INR886 crore total; growth ~44% with ~30% from volume. Hisense JV delivered ~35,000 ACs in Q1 (~60,000 in Jan-Jun season) for ~INR65 crore Q1 revenue (~INR120 crore for the season).

segments.name: SDA + LDA (small and large domestic appliances)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR130 crore vs ~INR80 crore last year per management; Q1 growth ~68% YoY. Gross margin reportedly 1.5-2 percentage points above AC (stated as 'basis points', likely a units slip). Washing machines: top-load fully automatic in production for 3 national/multinational brands; front-load pilot underway, mass production targeted by end-Sept/October 2026.

segments.name: Components
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 23% (question-referenced figure, not confirmed by management); components are largely AC-linked (controllers, cross-flow fans, copper tubing) and seasonal. Management said growth will continue and non-AC components are being explored.

guidance_outlook: Industry AC growth expected ~20% in FY27; management expects EPACK to outgrow the industry. No formal numerical guidance given on revenue.
Target utilisation of all three plants (Dehradun, Bhiwadi, Sri City) at 55-60% for FY27 average; management said more than 60% on average.
Q2 and Q3 have historically been loss-making; management targets stopping the 'bleeding' in these quarters within 4-6 quarters, but declined to say whether Q2 FY27 will be PAT positive.
PLI discount rollback: aim to reverse fully by end-FY27; PLI ends with FY27, and normalised EBITDA expected from FY28. Prior commentary: ~6.5% EBITDA ex-PLI for recent quarters.

Capex: total budget ~INR450-470 crore; ~INR330-350 crore booked; INR60-70 crore additional capex expected in the remaining nine months; depreciation not expected to rise significantly over next three quarters.
Hisense: cumulative expected revenue of ~INR8,000 crore over five years; management said on track for calendar 2026 and front-load washing machine production by end-October.
Andhra Pradesh MoU: INR1,085 crore investment over five years, ~35 acres allotted; state investment subsidy about 50% of capex over 10 years.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR10 crore; ~INR60 crore in CWIP expected to capitalise over the next two quarters.
Sri City plant utilisation close to 50% in Q1 FY27 vs under 25% previously reported; Dehradun and Bhiwadi utilisation above 85-90% in Q1.
FY26 utilisation: Dehradun and Bhiwadi ~55%, Sri City below 25%.
Washing machine and LDA capacity ramp flagged as fastest-growing; front-load washing machine pilot to mass production around end-Oct 2026.

Compressors: management said domestic compressor capacity installed and in pipeline (operational by end-December) is sufficient; imports allowed until end of calendar 2026. No plan for in-house compressor capacity in the near term.
demand_pricing: RAC: channel inventory considered largely liquidated after old-BEE-rated stock sell-through allowed until end-June 2026; management estimates industry inventory at 3.5-4 million units, the lowest acceptable level.

Pricing: contracts with large customers reset prices quarterly; most commodity pass-through completed with a time lag, and management said little price increase remains to be passed on. Forex was the main margin headwind.

Customer base: 72 customers and 19 product categories at FY26 close; ~73 customers and 19 product lines now, targeting ~75 customers and 20 product lines by end-FY27. Three new categories added in Q1, four more in pipeline.
Commodities: no forward hedging; back-to-back booking against confirmed orders, with changes passed through in the following quarter.
Inventory: in-house inventory mix roughly 70-75% AC and 25-30% non-AC; working capital days ~50-60, with inventory elevated due to BIS/QCO revisions.
